definitions.explanation: To engage in meaningful conversation with someone, often about personal matters or shared experiences.

examples.japanese: {友達|ともだち}と{夢|ゆめ}について{語|かた}り{合|あ}った。
examples.english: I talked with my friend about our dreams.

examples.japanese: {夜|よる}を{通|とお}して{語|かた}り{合|あ}う。
{二人|ふたり}は{将来|しょうらい}のことを{真剣|しんけん}に{語|かた}り{合|あ}った。
examples.english: The two of them had a serious conversation about the future.

examples.japanese: クラスメートと{思|おも}い{出|で}を{語|かた}り{合|あ}う{時間|じかん}は{楽|たの}しかった。
examples.english: The time spent talking about memories with classmates was enjoyable.

examples.japanese: {久|ひさ}しぶりに{会|あ}った{友人|ゆうじん}と、お{互|たが}いの{近況|きんきょう}を{語|かた}り{合|あ}った。
examples.english: After meeting a friend for the first time in a while, we talked about what we'd each been up to.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {自動詞|じどうし} (intransitive). Pattern: Xと{語|かた}り{合|あ}う (to talk with X).

{語|かた}り{合|あ}う is formed from {語|かた}る (to tell, narrate) + {合|あ}う (mutual action suffix). The {合|あ}う indicates both parties participating.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ～と{語|かた}り{合|あ}う (to talk with ~)
- ～について{語|かた}り{合|あ}う (to talk about ~)
- {夜|よる}を{徹|てっ}して{語|かた}り{合|あ}う (to talk all night long)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {語|かた}り{合|あ}う: to talk together (implies depth/meaning)
- {話|はな}し{合|あ}う: to discuss (more practical/decision-focused)
- {語|かた}る: to tell, narrate (one-directional)
